Definition: Ephron, the name of a Canaanite and of two places in Palestine
BiblicalUsage: Ephron the Hittite owned the field and the cave of Machpelah. Abraham bought them from him for four hundred shekels of silver — the first piece of the promised land owned outright, where Sarah was buried and where Abraham himself would lie.
TheologicalSignificance: A grave bought in faith is the beginning of the promise taking ground, held for a people who did not yet own the land. I believe Ephron's field matters because Abraham paid full price for it: faith does not take shortcuts, even with a grave.
